newsitem.title: UK: World oil refiner margins fall on week.
newsitem.headline: World oil refiner margins fall on week.

text.p: Oil refining margins fell last week in most major refining regions although steady declines from early June appeared to have been halted by the end of the week.
Average margins for refiners on the U.S. Gulf coast running Brent crude rose to $1.35 a barrel last week from $1.08 the previous week.
But margins fell on a weekly basis in all other regions, according to Reuters data calculated from standard product yields.
The Mediterranean was hardest hit, with delays in the resumption of Iraqi exports cited as a reason for high crude prices in the region.

Last week's average margins for simple hydroskimming refineries in the Med were 35 cents in the red last week, a fall of nearly 60 cents from the previous week, and some Med refiners even said they were mulling the possibility of cuts in throughput.
These Med margins had recovered slightly to minus 38 cents on Friday, but this was still very poor when compared to the +$1.94 calculated on June 9.

Margins for complex cracking refineries in Singapore running Dubai crudes fell to an average of $2.29 last week, a fall of 35 cents on the week, although by Friday these had recovered to just over $2.50.

But these compare poorly to levels approaching +$3.50 in early June. In response to poor margins, Shell Singapore cut throughputs last week by 15 percent. This follows Esso Singapore's decision the previous week to cut refining runs by 10 percent.
Margins in Rotterdam for complex refiners running Brent crude also recovered by the week's end to $1.39 a barrel, compared to the low of $0.92 reached on July 2.
But the recovery failed to boost margins back to the high levels seen on June 6 when profits were calculated at $2.78 for complex refiners and at $1.52 for simple hydroskimmers.
